label: Challenged classical patriarchal atomistic exegesis via tawhidic hermeneutics
description: Amina Wadud critiqued classical medieval jurisprudence and tafsir traditions exemplified by Al-Ghazali for enshrining hierarchal gender assumptions, proposing instead a holistic tawhidic paradigm grounded in horizontal human moral agency (khilafah).
dialecticalTension: Refutes hierarchical cosmic gender ontology while remaining grounded in Qur'anic monotheism.
historicalContext: Qur'an and Woman (1992) and Inside the Gender Jihad (2006).

citations.author: Amina Wadud
citations.work: Inside the Gender Jihad: Women's Reform in Islam

label: Applied philosophical hermeneutics of text, context, and horizon to sacred reading
description: Drawing on modern philosophical hermeneutics of textual world-disclosure and reader situatedness, Wadud distinguished universal ethical principles of the Qur'an from seventh-century Arabian patriarchal customs.
dialecticalTension: Bridges contemporary Continental hermeneutics with Fazlur Rahman's double-movement Islamic method.
